title: Apple-Fennel Pulled Pork with Cider Gravy
description: Lean shoulder pieces pull into short strands that catch a mellow apple and fennel gravy.
equipment: Small enamel Dutch oven with tight lid, sized to hold the food snugly

ingredients.name: lean boneless pork shoulder muscles
ingredients.note: Separate the butt into muscles, discard the fat cap and seams, and weigh only the lean pieces.

ingredients.name: low-sodium chicken broth
ingredients.note: Use plain broth made from meat, bones and water, with no added vegetable blend or seasonings.

ingredients.name: hot drinking water
ingredients.note: Keep ready; use only as needed to maintain liquid depth or make up the sauce measure.

steps.title: Heat the Traeger
steps.text: Preheat the Traeger Silverton 610 to 300°F with apple and hickory, mixed two parts apple to one part hickory pellets, about 15 minutes with the lid closed.

steps.title: Warm the braising liquid
steps.text: Bring {broth} with {cider}, {fennel} and {paprika} just to a simmer in the open Dutch oven on the stove, about 3–6 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the braising liquid
steps.text: Move the uncovered pot to the Traeger grate. Close the smoker lid and smoke the liquid for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Shorten the grain
steps.text: Cut {pork} across the grain into pieces about 1 inch wide.

steps.title: Seal the braise
steps.text: Set the pork in the smoked liquid. Add {topup} if needed to reach halfway up the pieces. Cover immediately with the lid. No temperature-triggered wrap is needed.

steps.title: Braise the shoulder
steps.text: Cook at 300°F for 1 3/4 to 2 3/4 hours. Start checking the largest pieces near 195°F and stop when a fork twists easily in several pieces. Keep the pork at least halfway submerged throughout.

steps.title: Rest in the juices
steps.text: Rest the covered pork off heat for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Pull into small pieces
steps.text: Lift the pork into a warm bowl and pull into short strands with two forks. Moisten with cooking liquid and cover.

steps.title: Measure the sauce base
steps.text: Skim excess fat from the braising liquid. Measure 1 1/2 cups into the HexClad skillet, topping up with {topup} if needed.

steps.title: Thicken the sauce
steps.text: Bring the skillet liquid to a boil. Whisk in the stirred slurry and simmer for 1 minute, stirring, until the sauce coats the back of a spoon.

steps.title: Dress the pork
steps.text: Fold the pulled pork into the gravy until every strand is coated. Divide among the bowls and spoon any sauce left in the skillet over them.

notes: Make ahead: Pull the pork while warm and chill in its finished gravy. Option A uses cider and vinegar. For gentler Option B, omit the vinegar and replace half the cider with additional plain broth. Refrigerate promptly in shallow portions and use within 3 days. Freezer-Friendly Verdict: Yes. Freeze individual portions surrounded by sauce for up to 2 months to protect their moisture. Fridge reheat: Warm one portion covered in its sauce in the HexClad over medium-low heat. Turn gently, adding a splash of water if needed. Check after 6 minutes and continue until the food reaches 165°F throughout. Freezer reheat: Thaw overnight in the refrigerator. Follow the fridge reheating directions and stir the sauce smooth.
